home.intro_1: Comprehensive assessment of hazardous effects caused by impacts of cosmic bodies
home.intro_3: Estimation of air-blast and radiation effects, crater and ejecta, seismic effect and atmospheric disturbances

density.label: Density
density.help: Density of cosmic body (kg/m<sup>3</sup>). It is assumed that asteroid density is in the range 2000-3320 kg/m<sup>3</sup>, cometary objects density is 500-1200 kg/m<sup>3</sup>

velocity.label: Velocity
velocity.help: Projectile entry velocity is in the range from 12 to 72 km/s

entry angle.label: Entry angle
entry angle.help: The projectile entry angle (i.e., the angle to the Earth's surface). Setting it to 90° means that the projectile falls vertically.

target type.label: Target Type
target type.help:
The target type determines the properties of the surface on which the cosmic body hits.
Density of a rock is 2650, sand: 1600 kg/m3

zero point.label: Zero Point
zero point.entry point 100km: Entry point at 100km above the ground
zero point.surface intersection: The point of intersection of the trajectory with the Earth's surface

entry vector.help:
The latitude and the longitude of the projectile entry point.
Both latitude and longitude are measured in degrees. Latitude ranges from -90° to 90°. Longitude ranges from -180° to 180°.

along across.label: along-across
along across.along help: L<sub>y</sub> The distance along the trajectory from the zero point to the point of intersection with the perpendicular drawn from the observation point to the projection of the trajectory
along across.across help: L<sub>x</sub> The length of the perpendicular drawn from the observation point to the projection of the trajectory of the cosmic body

distance angle.label: distance-angle
distance angle.distance help title: Distance to the Zero Point, L
distance angle.distance help: The distance between the point of effect and the zero point (L)
distance angle.angle help: The angle between the direction from the observation point to the zero point and the projection of the trajectory on the surface of the Earth (𝜓)

entry point 100km.help: The distance between the point of effect and the point of intersection of the trajectory with the Earth's surface

latitude longitude.label: latitude-longitude
latitude longitude.help title: Latitude and Longitude of the Zero Point
latitude longitude.help:
The latitude and the longitude of the zero point.
Both latitude and longitude are measured in degrees. Latitude ranges from -90° to 90°. Longitude ranges from -180° to 180°.

shockwave.description: Numerical simulations of a shock wave from the cosmic object impact provide possibility to suggest scaling relations for a value of maximal overpressure and its distribution on the surface, for maximal wind velocity behind the front and for a squares, where overpressure is larger than a fixed levelall values are determined based only on the properties of the impactor
shockwave.Distance to the center: Distance to the center of a overpressure field from the point of intersection of the trajectory with the Earth`s surface
shockwave.Areas: Areas, at which chosen levels of overpressure exceed
shockwave.The value of the overpressure: The value of the overpressure in the point of observation
shockwave.Maximum wind speed: Maximum wind speed behind the shock front in the point of observation

Effective altitude.body: The effective height Heff is the height at which the impactor loses most of its energy and slows down significantly, which makes it possible to determine the boundary between different scenarios (meteor explosion, transitional variant or crater-forming impact). As a first approximation, the overpressure in the shock wave from the falling cosmic body can be estimated by considering the explosion at the altitude Heff, the energy of which is determined by the energy of the falling body.

Maximal overpressure.body: Максимальное избыточное давление в атм и Па в точке максимального эффекта

Distance to the center.body: Расстояние до усредненного центра распределения избыточного давления от точки пересечения траектории с поверхностью Земли. Детально рассматривается в статье:

The value of the overpressure.body: Максимальное избыточное давление за фронтом ударной волны регистрируемое в точке наблюдения

Maximum wind speed.body: Максимальная скорость ветра за фронтом ударной волны регистрируемая в точке наблюдения

irradiation.description: One of the main hazardous effects of the cosmic body impacts
irradiation.Distance to the center: Distance to the center of a radiation field from the point of intersection of the trajectory with the Earth`s surface
irradiation.Thermal exposure in the point of observa: Maximal thermal exposure in the point of observation
irradiation.Thermal flux in the point of observation: Maximal thermal flux in the point of observation

Thermal exposure.body: Максимальная плотность тепловой энергии 𝑄(в Дж/см2), падающая на единичную площадку в указанной точке наблюдения, ориентированную на источник

Maximal thermal exposure.body: Максимальная плотность тепловой энергии 𝑄(в Дж/см2), падающая на единичную площадку, ориентированную на источник в эпицентре

Maximal irradiation flux.body: Максимальная поток излучения W(в Вт/см2), падающий на единичную площадку, ориентированную на источник в эпицентре

Radiation altitude.body: Эффективная радиационная высота(в км). Это высота, на которой можно расположить эквивалентный точечный источник (с энергией равной энергии ударника), который вызывает примерно те же радиационные последствия на больших расстояниях.

Radiation pulse duration.body: Длительность импульса излучения в секундах. Длительности радиационного импульса составляют от ~1 минуты при размере ударяющего тела 300 м до ~10 минут при размере 3 км.

Radiation efficiency.body: Эффективность высвета - доля кинетической энергии тела переходящая в тепловое излучение в процентах

Distance to the center.header: Расстояние от эпицентра до точки пересечения траектории с поверхностью Земли
Distance to the center.body: Расстояние от эпицентра (точки где наблюдается максимальный эффект) до точки пересечения траектории с поверхностью Земли

Thermal exposure in the point of observa.body: Максимальное значение плотности энергии излучения, падающей на единичную площадку, ориентированную на источник в точке наблюдения

Thermal flux in the point of observation.body: Максимальное значение радиационного потока, падающего на единичную площадку, ориентированную на источник в точке наблюдения

transient.description: Diameter and depth of a crater, which are set at the end of excavation stage, measured in relation to the level of the original surface

final.description: Final crater parameters are defined based on transient crater size.Also, final crater size and depth depend on its type (simple or complex).Simple called craters with final size less than 3 km in diameter (2.56km for corresponding transient diameter), complex – with final diameter more than 3 km (transient crater size more than 2.56 km).

melt.Melt target material in the crater count: Melt target material in the crater counting
melt.description: Breccia lens thickness (for simple crater) and thickness and volume of the melt layer

ejecta.description: Target and projectile material excavated from the crater is called ejecta. Ejected particles land around the crater forming ejecta deposit or ejecta blanket. A thickness of ejecta blanket is the greatest at the crater rim and decreases with distance from the crater. At high distances ejecta become patchy. We give an average thickness of the ejecta blanket and a thickness melted part of the ejecta blanket.
ejecta.Thickness of ejecta blanket: Thickness of ejecta blanket in the observational point
ejecta.Fraction of melt in ejecta: Fraction of melt in ejecta in the observational point

seismic.description: The seismic magnitude of the impact event is estimated for bothcrater forming impacts and aerial bursts.The magnitude is used for determination of the instrumental characteristics of a seismic disturbance in the observational point.
seismic.Richter scale magnitude of the impact ev: Richter scale magnitude of the impact event
seismic.Time of arrival to the observation point: Time of arrival to the observation point (started from moment of maximal energy deposition)

Richter scale magnitude of the impact ev.header: Richter scale magnitude of the impact event
Richter scale magnitude of the impact ev.body: Richter scale magnitude is determined from Gutenberg–Richter’s l formula. The seismic efficiency coefficient equals 10^-5 for bodies less than 100 m (aerial burst) and 10^-3  for bodies large than 300 m (crater forming impact).  The interpolation is used in the intermediate size interval.

Mercally scale intensity.body: Mercally scale intensity at the observational point

The peak ground velocity.body: The peak ground velocity at the observational point

The peak ground acceleration.body: The peak ground acceleration at the observational point

Time of arrival to the observation point.body: The time interval between impact and major seismic shaking at the observational point

atmospheric_disturbances.description: Atmospheric plume resulting from impact rises to high altitudes and generates atmospheric disturbances expanding to distances up to thousands of kilometres. To estimate these disturbances we consider deviations of air density from average value at an altitude of 300 km and deviations of temperature from equilibrium value at an altitude of 100 km.
atmospheric_disturbances.Peak amplitude of relative density oscil: Peak amplitude of relative density oscillations at an altitude of 300 km
atmospheric_disturbances.Peak amplitude of relative temperature o: Peak amplitude of relative temperature oscillations at an altitude of 100 km

Peak amplitude of relative density oscil.header: Peak amplitude of relative density oscillations at an altitude of 300 km
Peak amplitude of relative density oscil.body: Peak amplitude of relative density oscillations (dimensionless) at an altitude of 300 km is defined as an all-time maximum of ((ϱ(t,x,y)-ϱ0))/ϱ0 ,  where ϱ0 is an undisturbed air density at an altitude of 300 km, ϱ(t,x,y) is air density at the moment t at an altitude 300 km in the point with coordinates (x,y).

Peak amplitude of relative temperature o.header: Peak amplitude of relative temperature oscillations at an altitude of 100 km
Peak amplitude of relative temperature o.body: Peak amplitude of relative temperature oscillations (dimensionless) at an altitude of 100 km is defined as an all-time maximum of   ((T(t,x,y)-T0))/T0 , where T0 is an undisturbed air temperature at an altitude of 100 km, T(t,x,y) is air temperature at the moment t at an altitude 100 km in the point with coordinates (x,y).

schema.Entry direction: Direction from entry point at 100km above the ground
schema.Surface intersection point: The point of intersection of the trajectory with the Earth's surface
schema.Effective thermal point source: Position of effective thermal point source
